skill.name: commit
skill.description: Create conventional git commits with repository review, staging guidance, emoji prefixes, and consistent message style.
skill.summary: Create repository-aware conventional commits with clear messages and safe git workflow guidance.
skill.author: Codename-11

security_audit.summary: No confirmed security issue was found in the cited static findings. The detections are Markdown command examples, a documentation URL, and a safety rule warning against committing secret files.

static_findings.snippet: 1. **Check status**: Run `git status` to see changes
2. **Review diff**: Run `git diff` to understand changes
3. **Check recent commits**: Run `git log --oneline -5` for commit style reference
4. **Stage files**: If no files staged, add relevant files with `git add`
- NEVER commit files that may contain secrets (.env, credentials.json)
- NEVER commit files that may contain secrets (.env, credentials.json)

content.value_statement: Manual commits can be inconsistent and miss useful context. This skill reviews changes and drafts conventional commit messages for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Checks repository status before creating a commit.
Reviews diffs to understand changed files and intent.
Uses recent commit history as a style reference.
Stages relevant files when no files are staged.
Formats commit messages with conventional types and attribution.
Suggests separate commits for unrelated changes.
limitations: It depends on the current repository state and available git history.
It cannot guarantee that every secret-like file is excluded.
It should not amend pushed commits without explicit user approval.
It is focused on commits, not pull requests or release automation.

use_cases.title: Commit Completed Feature Work
use_cases.description: Review changed source files and create a conventional feature commit with a concise message.

use_cases.title: Save Documentation Updates
use_cases.description: Turn documentation edits into a clear docs commit that matches existing repository style.

use_cases.title: Organize Mixed Changes
use_cases.description: Identify unrelated changes and prepare separate commits when one commit would be unclear.

prompt_templates.title: Commit Current Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Please review my current repository changes and create one clear conventional commit.

prompt_templates.title: Match Repository Style
prompt_templates.scenario: Use recent history as a guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit these changes using the existing repository commit style and an appropriate conventional type.

prompt_templates.title: Split Unrelated Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the diff and split unrelated changes into separate conventional commits when that is cleaner.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Safe Commit Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect staged and unstaged changes, avoid secret files, and create the most appropriate conventional commit set.

output_examples.input: User asks to commit a new authentication feature.
output_examples.output: The assistant reviews status and diff, stages relevant files, and creates a feature commit with a concise message and attribution.
The assistant selects a documentation commit type and creates a message focused on changed guide content.

output_examples.input: User changed tests and source files for separate tasks.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends separate commits when changes cover unrelated concerns.

best_practices: Review the diff before accepting the final commit.
Keep unrelated changes in separate commits when possible.
Confirm staged files do not include secrets or generated noise.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to hide unrelated changes in one commit.
Do not bypass hooks unless the user explicitly approves it.
Do not commit environment or credential files.

faq.question: Does this skill push commits to a remote repository?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow focuses on local commit creation.

faq.question: Does it support conventional commit types?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps common change types to conventional commit prefixes.

faq.question: Can it create multiple commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends multiple commits when changes cover different concerns.

faq.question: How does it choose a commit message style?
faq.answer: It reviews recent commits and uses that history as a style reference.

faq.question: Does it protect secrets?
faq.answer: It warns against committing secret-like files, but users should still review staged files.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
